---
title: "My topic still feels too vague"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-28"
---

## Find the weakest link

Try explaining what you want to find out in two sentences. Where does the explanation become vague? You may need a clearer problem, a more focused question or a realistic way to get the evidence.

## Try this now

1. Describe the problem and who it affects.
2. Write what you want to do: describe, explain, compare, predict or estimate an effect.
3. Connect that question to the evidence and method it needs.
4. Make small feasibility checks for access, sampling, measurement and approvals before committing resources.
5. Compare continuing, narrowing the question, changing direction, pausing or stopping.

Use the [topic due-diligence canvas](../templates/topic-due-diligence.qmd) and [research-question stress test](../checklists/research-question-stress-test.qmd).

## What to take when asking

Bring a one-page account of the topic, what your checks found, two realistic alternatives and your recommendation.

## Stop or escalate

Do not commit major resources while essential access is only informal, the question cannot be answered by the proposed evidence, or the work creates uncontrolled harm.

## You are moving again when

You've written a provisional question, how you'll get the evidence, what it can establish and the next small test. You also know what result would make you stop or reconsider.
